voice.refText: Twice a week, you sell your plasma, the pale part of your blood. It's the most the law allows. That's the band. A thin strip you wear across your forehead. While you sleep, it lends your brain to a company. And it pays you, by the hour.

Nurse.describe: A low, brisk female alto: a clinic nurse in her forties at the end of a night shift. Dry and kind, practical, crisp clear diction, every word distinct, standard American English.

Broker.describe: A smooth male baritone: a salesman in a grey suit in his fifties. Unhurried and friendly, a little too calm, every word a quiet offer, crisp clear diction, every word distinct.

Brother.describe: A light, bright male tenor: a boy of about eighteen in his last year of school, the listener's younger brother. Quick, teasing and wry, warm underneath, crisp clear diction, every word distinct, casual modern American English.

Bridge woman.describe: A clear, warm female voice, a woman in her forties. Mezzo, natural and conversational.

Boss.describe: A cheerful male baritone: an office boss in his late forties. Hearty and pleased with himself, brisk, a grin in the voice, crisp clear diction, every word distinct.

Grandmother.describe: A bright female voice, an old soprano: a grandmother in her eighties next door. Delighted with herself, slow and satisfied, clear diction, every word distinct, a light Mexican Spanish accent.

Clerk.describe: A flat, deep male baritone: a warehouse door clerk in his thirties. Bored and blunt, short words, crisp clear diction, every word distinct.

Narrator end.refText: Tonight you'll lie down, and you'll be clocking in. You always were. The shift is yours.

lines.say: [Flat, bored, final; the thousandth time tonight] Rested ones only.
lines.speaker: Clerk

lines.text: So a night is worth twelve dollars, and he can't even sell that. But one offer hasn't fallen. The man in the grey suit comes back.
lines.say: [Cool, even, precise; stress twelve, that, one and back; a small lift on hasn't fallen] So a night is worth twelve dollars, and he can't even sell that. But one offer hasn't fallen. The man in the grey suit comes back.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The kitchen table. A premium contract. Triple pay, every night, all night, for a year. It clears what the family owes by spring. And no more Thursdays in the chair.
lines.say: [Cool, precise, the terms read out one by one; stress triple, every, all, spring and no more] The kitchen table. A premium contract. Triple pay, every night, all night, for a year. It clears what the family owes by spring. And no more Thursdays in the chair.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Sign, and nobody in this house sits in that chair again. Don't, and it's Thursday forever. You can't sleep on it. Sleeping is the job.
lines.say: [Cool, even, the tightest line in the film; stress Sign, Don't, forever, sleep and job; equal weight on all four sentences] Sign, and nobody in this house sits in that chair again. Don't, and it's Thursday forever. You can't sleep on it. Sleeping is the job.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: You pick up the pen.
lines.say: [Cool, quiet, one beat; stress pen] You pick up the pen.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Brother: Not yet. Look.
lines.say: [Urgent, hand slammed flat on the page, breath held; stress Look] Not yet. Look.
lines.speaker: Brother

lines.text: Six weeks of crumbs, his and yours. He thinks they add up to something.
lines.say: [Cool, even, a shade sceptical on the second sentence; stress six weeks and something] Six weeks of crumbs, his and yours. He thinks they add up to something.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Broker: Is that a shoe?
lines.say: [Politely baffled, head tilted, a real question] Is that a shoe?
lines.speaker: Broker

lines.text: Broker: Offer closes midnight.
lines.say: [Pleasant, unhurried, a door swinging shut; stress midnight] Offer closes midnight.
lines.speaker: Broker

lines.text: The kitchen clock. Eleven.
lines.say: [Cool, clipped, two facts; stress Eleven] The kitchen clock. Eleven.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The crumbs on the bed. His and yours.
lines.say: [Cool, quiet, precise; stress His and yours] The crumbs on the bed. His and yours.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The same face. Drawn badly, the same way.
lines.say: [Cool, even, dry; stress same both times and badly; the joke is in the word order, don't play it] The same face. Drawn badly, the same way.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He opens the laptop.
lines.say: [Cool, quiet, a hinge turning; stress opens] He opens the laptop.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: One brain, one band, one jar, the leaflet said. Each brain stays its own.
lines.say: [Cool, precise, quoting; stress one three times and own; a hair of doubt on said] One brain, one band, one jar, the leaflet said. Each brain stays its own.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: There was never one of anything. You never lost anything alone. For eight hours a night, every sleeper on the band was one mind.
lines.say: [Cool, even, the pieces locking into place; stress never, alone, every and one mind; slow the last three words] There was never one of anything. You never lost anything alone. For eight hours a night, every sleeper on the band was one mind.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In 2020, over a million people lent their idle home computers to one project.
lines.say: [cool, even, precise; a stress on a million] In twenty twenty, over a million people lent their idle home computers to one project.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The scientists behind it say it became the first computer to pass a billion billion sums a second.
lines.say: [cool, even, precise, quiet awe; a stress on first, a pause before a billion billion] The scientists behind it say it became the first computer to pass a billion billion sums a second.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Spare machines, linked into one. Now spare brains.
lines.say: [cool, slow, a pause between the two sentences, a stress on brains] Spare machines, linked into one. Now spare brains.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Brother: So what did we get?
lines.say: [hushed, amazed, crisp and clear, the old joke turned into wonder, a stress on we] So what did we get?
lines.speaker: Brother

lines.text: So what's the job? The crumbs fit together. Into a drawing. And the drawing is a machine.
lines.say: [Cool, even, each sentence a step closer; stress job, fit, drawing and machine; a half-beat before machine] So what's the job? The crumbs fit together. Into a drawing. And the drawing is a machine.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Why didn't the company just use a computer? Nobody's built one that can. Yet. That's the job.
lines.say: [Cool, precise, the loophole shut; stress can, Yet and job; Yet alone, a full stop either side of it] Why didn't the company just use a computer? Nobody's built one that can. Yet. That's the job.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The job the sleepers are paid for is to design the thing that will never need sleepers.
lines.say: [Cool, even, no colour added; stress design, never and sleepers; let the sentence land on its own] The job the sleepers are paid for is to design the thing that will never need sleepers.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The biggest idea people ever had together, and nobody was awake for it.
lines.say: [Cool, quiet, awe held just under the surface; stress biggest, together and awake] The biggest idea people ever had together, and nobody was awake for it.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Eleven fifty-eight. The pen in one hand. The band in the other, its teal light on.
lines.say: [Warmer now, still exact, the tempo lifting; stress fifty-eight, pen, band and on] Eleven fifty-eight. The pen in one hand. The band in the other, its teal light on.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: You remember nothing of your nights. Only the crumbs. And now you know what they were building. You'd rather sit in that chair every Thursday than build it every night.
lines.say: [Warm, certain, the lesson; stress nothing, know, chair, every Thursday and every night; the last sentence said with a smile, a decision already made] You remember nothing of your nights. Only the crumbs. And now you know what they were building. You'd rather sit in that chair every Thursday than build it every night.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: Brother: Scam. Told you.
lines.say: [Vindicated, grinning, six weeks of waiting paid off; stress Told] Scam. Told you.
lines.speaker: Brother

lines.text: Brother: Come back Thursday.
lines.say: [A whisper through cupped hands, delighted with himself, barely holding the laugh; stress Thursday] Come back Thursday.
lines.speaker: Brother

lines.text: The man in the grey suit, at midnight, for your answer. Nobody opens.
lines.say: [Warm, dry, quietly triumphant; stress midnight, answer and Nobody] The man in the grey suit, at midnight, for your answer. Nobody opens.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: You lie down with nothing on your forehead. The offer's gone. Yours is the only window on the street not working.
lines.say: [Warm, easy, proud; stress nothing, gone, only and not working; the last sentence a quiet brag] You lie down with nothing on your forehead. The offer's gone. Yours is the only window on the street not working.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: And for the first time in six weeks, nobody's typing.
lines.say: [Warm, soft, relieved; stress first and nobody's; let the silence after it sit] And for the first time in six weeks, nobody's typing.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: You wake. You know your street. You remember yesterday: his face over the notebook.
lines.say: [Warm, bright, morning in the voice; stress know, remember and his face] You wake. You know your street. You remember yesterday: his face over the notebook.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: And one dream that was only yours. A bridge, in your own colours. Nobody else dreamt it.
lines.say: [Warm, glad, a secret kept; stress only yours, own and Nobody else] And one dream that was only yours. A bridge, in your own colours. Nobody else dreamt it.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: Brother: What'd you get, then?
lines.say: [Teasing, palm out, already knowing the answer; stress then] What'd you get, then?
lines.speaker: Brother

lines.text: Nothing. The best deal on the street, and you're the only one taking it.
lines.say: [Warm, triumphant, a grin in it; stress Nothing, best and only one] Nothing. The best deal on the street, and you're the only one taking it.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: Tonight you'll lie down, and you'll be clocking in. You always were. The shift is yours.
lines.say: [Warm, triumphant, the thesis of the film; stress clocking in, always and yours; slow the last three words] Tonight you'll lie down, and you'll be clocking in. You always were. The shift is yours.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: Thursday. The clinic steps.
lines.say: [Warm, light, a smile on the word; stress Thursday] Thursday. The clinic steps.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: Broker: This one's for daytime.
lines.say: [Pleasant, unbothered, a salesman who has never lost a sale; stress daytime] This one's for daytime.
lines.speaker: Broker

lines.text: Broker: Everyone else already said yes.
lines.say: [Pleasant, friendly, called after you with no threat in it at all; stress Everyone and already] Everyone else already said yes.
lines.speaker: Broker

lines.text: Nobody's asleep. And everybody's typing.
lines.say: [Warm but level, the twist, no alarm; stress Nobody's and everybody's; the same tune as nobody's typing, turned over] Nobody's asleep. And everybody's typing.
lines.speaker: Narrator end

lines.text: So, would you rent your nights? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.say: [Warm, direct, back to the viewer; stress you, same, like and subscribe] So, would you rent your nights? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.speaker: Narrator end
